title: Encore: How living with secrets can harm you, with Michael Slepian, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a summer break, so we're rerunning some of our favorite episodes from the paSt. In 2022, I talked to psychologist Michael Slepian about why people
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》节目正在休暑假，所以我们重播了一些过去最受欢迎的剧集。2022年，我采访了心理学家迈克尔·斯莱皮安（Michael Slepian），探讨了人们为什么

sentences.en: keep secrets, why keeping a secret bottled up inside can be harmful, and how keeping secrets and sharing them affect people's relationships with each other.
sentences.zh: 会保守秘密，将秘密憋在心里为何有害，以及保守秘密和分享秘密如何影响人际关系。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoyed this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: We'll be back with new episodes beginning August 26th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于8月26日带着新剧集回归。

sentences.en: Do you have secrets?
sentences.zh: 你有秘密吗？

sentences.en: Maybe you're looking to leave your job and don't want your co-workers or your boss to know.
sentences.zh: 也许你正打算辞职，但不想让同事或老板知道。

sentences.en: Maybe you still feel shame about cheating on an exam in high school.
sentences.zh: 也许你对高中考试作弊的事至今仍感到羞愧。

sentences.en: Maybe you haven't told anyone whom you voted for in the last election.
sentences.zh: 也许你还没告诉任何人你在上次选举中投给了谁。

sentences.en: Or perhaps a friend told you about an extramarital affair and swore you to secrecy.
sentences.zh: 又或者，一位朋友告诉你他有婚外情，并让你发誓保密。

sentences.en: We keep our own secrets, and sometimes we keep those of others.
sentences.zh: 我们既有自己的秘密，有时也要保守他人的秘密。

sentences.en: Research has shown that on average, people have about 13 secrets at any one time, five of which they have never told another person.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，人们平均同时拥有约13个秘密，其中5个从未告诉过任何人。

sentences.en: How does this secret keeping affect us?
sentences.zh: 这种保守秘密的行为如何影响我们？

sentences.en: People often describe secrets as burdens that weigh them down or eat away at them.
sentences.zh: 人们常把秘密描述为压在心头或蚕食内心的负担。

sentences.en: Do these metaphors reflect a deeper truth?
sentences.zh: 这些隐喻是否反映了更深层的真相？

sentences.en: Does keeping a secret bottled up inside harm us?
sentences.zh: 将秘密憋在心里会伤害我们吗？

sentences.en: And if so, how?
sentences.zh: 如果是，又是如何伤害的？

sentences.en: How does keeping secrets or sharing them affect people's relationships with each other?
sentences.zh: 保守秘密或分享秘密如何影响人与人之间的关系？

sentences.en: How do we decide whom we can trust with our secrets?
sentences.zh: 我们如何决定谁值得托付秘密？

sentences.en: And can other people tell when we're holding something back?
sentences.zh: 当我们在隐瞒某事时，别人能看出来吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Michael Slepian, the Sanford C.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是迈克尔·斯莱皮安博士，他是桑福德·C·伯恩斯坦公司（Sanford C. Bernstein and Company）的领导力与伦理学副教授，

sentences.en: Bernstein and Company Associate Professor of Leadership and Ethics at Columbia Business School.
sentences.zh: 任职于哥伦比亚大学商学院。

sentences.en: He's a research psychologist who studies the psychology of secrets.
sentences.zh: 他是一位研究秘密心理学的研究型心理学家。

sentences.en: He examines the intersection of secrecy, trust, and motivation, including the consequences of secrecy and how we judge and
sentences.zh: 他研究保密、信任与动机的交叉领域，包括保密的后果以及我们如何判断和

sentences.en: develop truSt. His new book, The Secret Life of Secrets, How Our Inner Worlds Shape Well-Being,
sentences.zh: 建立信任。他的新书《秘密的秘密生活：我们的内心世界如何塑造幸福、

sentences.en: Relationships, and Who We Are, is being released in June by Penguin Random House.
sentences.zh: 人际关系以及我们是谁》（The Secret Life of Secrets, How Our Inner Worlds Shape Well-Being, Relationships, and Who We Are）将于6月由企鹅兰登书屋出版。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Slepian.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加我们的节目，斯莱皮安博士。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: So let's start with the number I quoted in the introduction, that people keep about 13 secrets at any one time on average, and five of them they've never told anyone.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从我在开场白中引用的数字开始：人们平均同时保守着约13个秘密，其中5个从未告诉过任何人。

sentences.en: Those numbers come from your research.
sentences.zh: 这些数字来自您的研究。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that study?
sentences.zh: 能跟我们讲讲那项研究吗？

sentences.en: How did you arrive at those numbers?
sentences.zh: 您是如何得出这些数字的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So when we first started this research, we didn't know, we didn't have the most basic questions yet answered, like what secrets do people keep?
sentences.zh: 当我们刚开始这项研究时，我们还不知道，甚至连最基本的问题都没有答案，比如人们保守的都是些什么秘密？

sentences.en: How often did they keep them?
sentences.zh: 他们保守秘密的频率如何？

sentences.en: And so we went to find out.
sentences.zh: 于是我们去寻找答案。

sentences.en: We asked a couple thousand people, what is the secret you're currently keeping right now?
sentences.zh: 我们询问了几千人：你现在保守的秘密是什么？

sentences.en: We looked at the responses and looked at the themes and the common instances listed, and we saw 38
sentences.zh: 我们查看了回复，分析了主题和列举的常见实例，发现有38个

sentences.en: categories could really well capture what those folks said that they were keeping secret.
sentences.zh: 类别可以很好地涵盖这些人所说的秘密。

sentences.en: And then when we gave this list to another group of participants, sure enough, 97% of them say they
sentences.zh: 然后，当我们把这份清单交给另一组参与者时，果然，97%的人说他们

sentences.en: have at least one of the secrets from the list right now, and the average person has 13 of the secrets from that list at any given time, five of which they've never told anyone.
sentences.zh: 现在至少拥有清单上的一个秘密，平均每个人同时拥有清单上的13个秘密，其中5个从未告诉过任何人。

sentences.en: And so these categories that we're talking about, they really comprehensively cover what people keep secret.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的这些类别，确实全面涵盖了人们保守的秘密。

sentences.en: When we ask people open-ended, what is the secret that you're keeping?
sentences.zh: 当我们以开放式问题询问人们“你保守的秘密是什么”时，

sentences.en: 92% of the time, it fits one of these categories.
sentences.zh: 92%的情况下，它都符合这些类别之一。

sentences.en: So what are some of the most common secrets that people keep?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们保守的最常见的秘密有哪些？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the most common secrets include having told a lie, and you don't want that to become known.
sentences.zh: 最常见的秘密包括撒过谎，而且你不希望别人知道。

sentences.en: Romantic desire, while you're not in a relationship, is a very common secret.
sentences.zh: 单身时的浪漫渴望，是一个非常普遍的秘密。

sentences.en: Money is another common secret, things related to sex.
sentences.zh: 金钱是另一个常见的秘密，还有与性相关的事情。

sentences.en: So how do you define a secret?
sentences.zh: 那么，您如何定义“秘密”？

sentences.en: Is there a difference, for instance, between a secret and something that we just consider private?
sentences.zh: 例如，秘密与我们仅仅认为是“隐私”的东西之间有什么区别吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: And in fact, there can be some gray area between, but there's a way to draw a line between
sentences.zh: 事实上，两者之间确实存在一些灰色地带，但有一种方法可以划清界限，

sentences.en: the two, which is that privacy tends to sort of focus on, you know, you don't broadcast personal information very, very widely if you're a private person.
sentences.zh: 那就是隐私往往侧重于——如果你是一个注重隐私的人，你就不会广泛地传播个人信息。

sentences.en: And if there's something that people don't know, it may be because these aren't the kinds of things we tend to talk about.
sentences.zh: 如果有些事情别人不知道，那可能是因为这些不是我们通常会谈论的话题。

sentences.en: So for a lot of folks, they don't talk about money, or they don't talk about sex.
sentences.zh: 所以对很多人来说，他们不谈论金钱，或者不谈论性。

sentences.en: And so that might be why people don't know those things about you.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是别人不知道你这些事情的原因。

sentences.en: But when it becomes a secret, it's not just that someone doesn't know this thing about you, but it's that you intend for them to not learn this information.
sentences.zh: 但当它成为一个秘密时，不仅仅是别人不知道关于你的这件事，而是你打算让他们不去了解这些信息。

sentences.en: That's when we arrive at a secret.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们定义秘密的时刻。

sentences.en: So let's talk for a minute about the intersection between lying and keeping a secret.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈撒谎和保守秘密之间的交叉点。

sentences.en: For instance, I recently watched the movie Dear Evan Hansen, where Evan creates this whole complicated fiction about having been friends with a schoolmate who has killed himself.
sentences.zh: 例如，我最近看了电影《致埃文·汉森》（Dear Evan Hansen），片中埃文编造了一个复杂的谎言，说自己曾是某位自杀同学的朋友。

sentences.en: The lies that Evan tells about the relationship are, they're very much like secrets, and they appear to be a heavy burden on
sentences.zh: 埃文关于这段关系的谎言，非常像秘密，而且它们似乎成了他沉重的负担，

sentences.en: him, much like secrets tend to be, only maybe more so because he never was friends with the other boy.
sentences.zh: 就像秘密往往会带来的那样，甚至可能更严重，因为他从未与那个男孩做过朋友。

sentences.en: So are lies just a different type of secret?
sentences.zh: 所以，谎言只是另一种类型的秘密吗？

sentences.en: So no, I would say that lying is one way you could keep a secret, but it's not the only way.
sentences.zh: 不，我会说撒谎是保守秘密的一种方式，但不是唯一方式。

sentences.en: There's plenty of secrets you can keep without telling lies.
sentences.zh: 有很多秘密你可以在不撒谎的情况下保守。

sentences.en: So a lie is one way out of many to keep a secret.
sentences.zh: 所以谎言只是保守秘密的众多方式之一。

sentences.en: And then, of course, you can keep a lie a secret, but they're sort of different constructs, but they're kind of intersecting in this way.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以把谎言当作秘密来保守，它们是不同的概念，但以这种方式相互交织。

sentences.en: So a lot of your work has to do with how secrets affect us, often in harmful ways.
sentences.zh: 您的很多工作都与秘密如何影响我们有关，通常是以有害的方式。

sentences.en: There's a line in an essay you wrote that said, the real problem with having secrets is not that we have to hide them, but rather that we have to live with them.
sentences.zh: 您写的一篇文章中有一句话说：“拥有秘密的真正问题不在于我们必须隐藏它们，而在于我们必须与它们共存。”

sentences.en: So why is living with secrets so difficult?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么与秘密共存如此困难？

sentences.en: What's so difficult about just simply having a secret, a secret that you might not ever have to
sentences.zh: 仅仅拥有一个秘密有什么难的？如果你在谈话中可能永远不需要隐藏它，

sentences.en: hide in conversation, if it's something you care about, or if it's something that's bothering you, to choose to be alone with that thing tends to not help.
sentences.zh: 如果那是你在意的事，或者困扰你的事，选择独自面对它往往无济于事。

sentences.en: We tend to not develop the healthiest ways of thinking about these struggles we keep entirely to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 对于这些完全藏在心里的挣扎，我们往往无法形成最健康的思考方式。

sentences.en: And so even whether you're hiding it frequently or not, your mind is going to return to this thing time and time again, and you're not going to know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论你是否频繁地隐藏它，你的大脑都会一次又一次地回到这件事上，而你却不知道该拿它怎么办。

sentences.en: Are there some types of secrets that are harder to live with at others?
sentences.zh: 有些类型的秘密是否比其他秘密更难共存？

sentences.en: For example, you've looked at the difference between secrets that people consider shameful and those they feel guilty about.
sentences.zh: 例如，您研究过人们认为“羞耻”的秘密与感到“内疚”的秘密之间的区别。

sentences.en: Is one worse than the other?
sentences.zh: 其中一个比另一个更糟糕吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in one sense, if we sort of ignored what our secrets are about, we could see that the secrets that return to our minds more frequently are the ones that
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，如果我们忽略秘密的内容，我们会发现那些更频繁地回到我们脑海中的秘密，

sentences.en: are also related to low well-being.
sentences.zh: 也与低幸福感有关。

sentences.en: Not the ones that we say we can see more frequently.
sentences.zh: 而不是那些我们说自己更频繁看到的秘密。

sentences.en: But when we look to what the secrets are about, we see this distinction that you mentioned between shame and guilt.
sentences.zh: 但当我们审视秘密的内容时，我们看到了您提到的羞耻感和内疚感之间的区别。

sentences.en: And shame, we can consider someone, when someone feels ashamed, they feel like I'm a bad person to some degree.
sentences.zh: 羞耻感，我们可以认为，当一个人感到羞耻时，他们在某种程度上觉得自己是个坏人。

sentences.en: When someone feels guilty, they think I've done a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 当一个人感到内疚时，他们认为我做了一件坏事。

sentences.en: And so instead of thinking I'm a bad person, I've done a bad thing is actually much more healthy.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其认为“我是个坏人”，不如认为“我做了一件坏事”，这实际上要健康得多。

sentences.en: And it's when people feel like I'm a bad person that they find their minds returning to the secret time and time again.
sentences.zh: 当人们觉得“我是个坏人”时，他们会发现自己的思绪一次又一次地回到那个秘密上。

sentences.en: And those are the secrets we say sort of hurt our well-being the moSt.
sentences.zh: 而那些正是我们所说的最损害我们幸福感的秘密。

sentences.en: And how does keeping secrets harm us?
sentences.zh: 那么保守秘密是如何伤害我们的呢？

sentences.en: Was there research that ties secrecy directly to poorer physical or mental health?
sentences.zh: 是否有研究将保密直接与较差的身体或心理健康联系起来？

sentences.en: So this is where things get tricky.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题变得棘手的地方。

sentences.en: Trying to link a specific secret to lower physical health is tough.
sentences.zh: 试图将特定的秘密与较低的身体健康联系起来是很困难的。

sentences.en: And so there was a well-known study in the 90s that looked at men who were keeping their sexual orientation secret who were also diagnosed with AIDS.
sentences.zh: 90年代有一项著名的研究，观察了那些保守自己性取向秘密且被诊断出患有艾滋病的男性。

sentences.en: And they found that the men who concealed their sexual orientation more often had a more rapid progression of disease and even died sooner.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，那些更频繁隐瞒性取向的男性，疾病进展更快，甚至死亡更早。

sentences.en: And so that's sort of a sobering idea.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个发人深省的观点。

sentences.en: But it doesn't mean it was the hiding part that was so bothersome or troubling.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着是“隐藏”这一部分让人感到如此困扰或麻烦。

sentences.en: There's the moment in which you sort of conceal a secret during conversation that turns out to be easier than we've made it out to be.
sentences.zh: 在谈话中隐瞒秘密的那一刻，其实比我们想象的要容易。

sentences.en: But the real problem with this situation is not feeling comfortable enough to be yourself.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况的真正问题在于，没有感到足够舒适去展现真实的自我。

sentences.en: And that's really very reliably related to lower well-being, feeling unsupported.
sentences.zh: 这确实与较低的幸福感和缺乏支持感有着非常可靠的联系。

sentences.en: And so it's having your mind return to ideas like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，让你的思绪回到这样的想法中：

sentences.en: I can't be who I am.
sentences.zh: “我无法做真实的自己。”

sentences.en: I'm not supported for who I am.
sentences.zh: “我真实的自我没有得到支持。”

sentences.en: That seems to be where the trouble or where the harm really begins.
sentences.zh: 这似乎才是麻烦或伤害真正开始的地方。

sentences.en: So is there a difference between keeping our own secrets and keeping a secret for someone else,
sentences.zh: 那么，保守我们自己的秘密与为他人保守秘密之间有什么区别吗？

sentences.en: such as one example I gave in the introduction about a friend who confesses an affair?
sentences.zh: 比如我在开场白中提到的那个朋友坦白婚外情的例子？

sentences.en: Does keeping someone else's secrets feel as burdensome as keeping our own?
sentences.zh: 为别人保守秘密会像保守自己的秘密一样让人感到负担吗？

sentences.en: It can.
sentences.zh: 可能会。

sentences.en: So if someone confides a secret in you and you have totally overlapping social networks, you're now essentially keeping the secret for them too.
sentences.zh: 如果有人向你吐露秘密，而你们的社交圈完全重叠，那么你本质上也在为他们保守秘密。

sentences.en: Or if only certain people are allowed to know, it can get burdensome really quickly.
sentences.zh: 或者如果只有特定的人被允许知道，它很快就会变得沉重。

sentences.en: But if it's something that's not directly relevant to some folks in your shared social network, it's not as difficult.
sentences.zh: 但如果这件事与你共同社交圈中的某些人没有直接关联，就不会那么困难。

sentences.en: When another person's secret becomes burdensome is when it becomes something we find our minds returning to time and time again.
sentences.zh: 当他人的秘密变得沉重时，是因为我们发现自己的思绪一次又一次地回到它上面。

sentences.en: But there's a good side too.
sentences.zh: 但也有好的一面。

sentences.en: We feel glad that other people feel comfortable confiding in us.
sentences.zh: 我们感到高兴，因为别人觉得可以放心地向我们吐露心声。

sentences.en: We see that as an act of intimacy that brings us closer together.
sentences.zh: 我们将此视为一种亲密行为，使我们更加亲近。

sentences.en: So sharing a secret then can bring people closer together?
sentences.zh: 那么，分享秘密可以让人更亲近吗？

sentences.en: Or does it depend on the nature of the secret or even the person to whom you've told it?
sentences.zh: 还是说这取决于秘密的性质，甚至取决于你告诉的对象？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I mean, I'm imagining you're telling someone that you're already close to you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想象你是在告诉一个你已经很亲近的人。

sentences.en: If it's someone you're not already close to, it would be quite intimate perhaps to reveal something
sentences.zh: 如果对方是你本来就不亲近的人，透露一些你不会随便告诉别人的事情，

sentences.en: that you wouldn't tell just anyone.
sentences.zh: 可能会非常亲密。

sentences.en: But again, it's a really great way to jumpstart a relationship.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这是开启一段关系的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: Anyone who's trying to form a relationship quickly realizes that sort of revealing sensitive things, making yourself vulnerable is a way to connect with each other.
sentences.zh: 任何试图建立关系的人很快就会意识到，透露敏感的事情，让自己变得脆弱，是彼此建立联系的一种方式。

sentences.en: What advice do you have for people who are living with secrets that are weighing on them?
sentences.zh: 对于那些正背负着秘密生活的人，您有什么建议？

sentences.en: How can they think about whether the risk of telling the secrets are worth the relief of being able to unburden themselves?
sentences.zh: 他们该如何权衡：说出秘密的风险是否值得通过卸下负担来获得解脱？

sentences.en: So this is a question that is just so hard to answer on your own.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难独自回答的问题。

sentences.en: And the good news is you don't have to.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，你不需要独自面对。

sentences.en: So you can still keep the secret from the person you're keeping it from.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以对那个你不想告知的人保守秘密。

sentences.en: But you can talk to a third party and say, like, what do you think I should do with this?
sentences.zh: 但你可以找第三方谈谈，问问他们：“你觉得我该怎么处理这件事？”

sentences.en: It's so helpful to just have one more perspective than your own, because it's really hard to step outside of your perspective, especially when you're not sure what to do.
sentences.zh: 能拥有除自己之外的另一个视角是非常有帮助的，因为当你不知道该怎么办时，很难跳出自己的视角。

sentences.en: Talking to a third party is definitely what I would recommend in that situation.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我绝对建议找第三方谈谈。

sentences.en: So you participated in a kind of public art project a few years ago where people could tell their secrets anonymously in a public phone installed in a park.
sentences.zh: 几年前您参与了一个公共艺术项目，人们可以在公园里安装的公共电话中匿名讲述自己的秘密。

sentences.en: Does that kind of anonymous sharing have the same effect?
sentences.zh: 那种匿名分享有同样的效果吗？

sentences.en: Will it make people feel better if you have a secret that you aren't ready to share with your friends or family?
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个还没准备好告诉朋友或家人的秘密，这样做会让人感觉好些吗？

sentences.en: Is it helpful to tell it to a stranger or even write it in a diary or a journal?
sentences.zh: 把秘密告诉陌生人，甚至写在日记里会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: If you're truly not ready to tell anyone that you know, or you just can't find yourself ready to talk about it, then something like this is a good start.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的还没准备好告诉任何你认识的人，或者就是无法让自己开口谈论它，那么像这样的方式是一个好的开始。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say it's everything, but it's a good start.
sentences.zh: 我不会说它是万能的，但这是一个好的开始。

sentences.en: Sometimes it just takes saying it out loud to feel like,
sentences.zh: 有时只需要把它大声说出来，就会觉得：

sentences.en: okay, this is something I can deal with or work on.
sentences.zh: “好吧，这是我可以处理或解决的事情。”

sentences.en: So whether you're doing that on the secret telephone, if you happen to stumble upon it in New York City, or journaling.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论你是通过那个秘密电话——如果你碰巧在纽约市偶然发现它的话——还是通过写日记来做这件事。

sentences.en: But journaling, you want to be careful.
sentences.zh: 但写日记时，你要小心。

sentences.en: Because in theory, it could be this great space to work through something on your own without involving another person.
sentences.zh: 因为理论上，这可以是一个无需他人参与、独自理清思绪的绝佳空间。

sentences.en: But if you're using the space to simply rehash the past, it can essentially become a written record of harmful rumination.
sentences.zh: 但如果你只是利用这个空间来反复咀嚼过去，它本质上可能会变成有害反刍的文字记录。

sentences.en: And that's when it actually harms more than it helps.
sentences.zh: 而那时的伤害反而大于帮助。

sentences.en: And so to get journaling to work, you really want to use it as a space to step outside of your usual perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以，要让写日记发挥作用，你真的需要把它当作一个跳出常规视角去思考的空间。

sentences.en: The thing that's extremely hard to do on your own, really easy to do in conversation with another person.
sentences.zh: 这在独自一人时极难做到，但在与他人的对话中却非常容易实现。

sentences.en: So what did you find from that phone project?
sentences.zh: 那么您从那个电话项目中发现了什么？

sentences.en: What were you asking people after they told their secrets?
sentences.zh: 人们讲完秘密后，您会问他们什么？

sentences.en: I assume there was some kind of follow-up?
sentences.zh: 我假设会有某种后续？

sentences.en: This is what it becomes.
sentences.zh: 这就是它最终的样子。

sentences.en: I wanted it to become a research project, but so far, it's an art project.
sentences.zh: 我本想把它做成一个研究项目，但到目前为止，它更像是一个艺术项目。

sentences.en: We haven't, you know, the idea was that we would program the phone so people could answer a few questions.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有，你知道，最初的想法是我们给电话编程，让人们可以回答几个问题。

sentences.en: That hasn't happened yet.
sentences.zh: 但这还没实现。

sentences.en: But we've just been looking at the things people keep secret.
sentences.zh: 但我们一直在观察人们保守的秘密。

sentences.en: And they're just, they're quite interesting to listen to.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实非常有趣。

sentences.en: And, you know, I've been doing this research for 10 years and hearing the person's voice describe the secret is a really interesting experience.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我做这项研究已经10年了，听当事人亲口描述他们的秘密，是一种非常有趣的体验。

sentences.en: I think they do something like that at Burning Man, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我想他们在“火人节”上做过类似的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Or they have in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 或者过去做过。

sentences.en: The phone in the desert.
sentences.zh: 沙漠里的电话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what about telling your secrets to a therapist?
sentences.zh: 那么，向治疗师倾诉秘密怎么样？

sentences.en: Is that sharing part of what makes therapy work for people?
sentences.zh: 这种分享是心理治疗对人们有效的一部分吗？

sentences.en: It's certainly one of the ingredients, for sure.
sentences.zh: 这当然是其中的要素之一，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And if that's something that you feel you'd be comfortable doing, if that might work for you, it's a great way to talk about these things
sentences.zh: 如果这是你觉得可以接受的事情，如果这可能对你有用，那么这是一个谈论这些事情的好方法，

sentences.en: without any of the risks that normally come with talking about these things to friends or family or your romantic partner even.
sentences.zh: 而且没有任何通常与朋友、家人甚至恋人谈论这些事情时所带来的风险。

sentences.en: But if that's not something you're interested in, really anyone can do this.
sentences.zh: 但如果你对此不感兴趣，其实任何人都可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Like anyone can sort of hear you out and say, that sucks, or I'm here for you.
sentences.zh: 就像任何人都可以倾听你的心声，说一句“那太糟糕了”或者“我会支持你”。

sentences.en: Most folks can offer just a little bit of advice that you hadn't considered because they have this unique perspective that is not your own.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都能提供一点你没考虑过的建议，因为他们拥有你所不具备的独特视角。

sentences.en: So any person you would feel comfortable talking to, our research shows that the typical response to being confided in is a positive response.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于任何你觉得可以放心交谈的人，我们的研究表明，被倾诉者的典型反应是积极的。

sentences.en: And someone has to respond very negatively for you to regret doing so.
sentences.zh: 而且，除非对方反应非常消极，否则你不会后悔这样做。

sentences.en: So even a lukewarm response, people find helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是平淡的反应，人们也会觉得有帮助。

sentences.en: What about people whose jobs require them to keep secrets?
sentences.zh: 那么那些工作要求保密的人呢？

sentences.en: And I don't mean the proprietary information, but people who are spies, for example, or journalists who agree to protect their
sentences.zh: 我指的不是商业机密，而是那些间谍，或者同意保护消息来源而宁愿坐牢的记者，

sentences.en: sources on pain of going to jail, or lawyers who might represent somebody they know is guilty.
sentences.zh: 又或者是那些可能为明知有罪的人辩护的律师。

sentences.en: Is keeping a secret because of your job the same as keeping a more personal secret?
sentences.zh: 因为工作而保守秘密，和保守个人秘密是一回事吗？

sentences.en: They can converge.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会重合。

sentences.en: When it's something that is on your mind a lot, but you're not allowed to tell your spouse, that becomes a difficult situation.
sentences.zh: 当某件事一直萦绕在心头，但你又不能告诉配偶时，这就成了一种困难的处境。

sentences.en: And it can feel isolating.
sentences.zh: 而且会让人感到孤立。

sentences.en: We see in our research, it can feel isolating to not be able to talk about your work with other people.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究发现，无法与他人谈论工作确实会让人感到孤立。

sentences.en: But there are some differences, as you might imagine, too.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所想，它们之间也存在一些差异。

sentences.en: If the nature of the secret you keep for work is, it's not something you have to think about a lot.
sentences.zh: 如果工作秘密的性质是那种你不需要过多思考的事情，

sentences.en: It seems not to be very burdensome.
sentences.zh: 那似乎就不会造成太大的负担。

sentences.en: But if it's something big, and you can't talk about it with other folks,
sentences.zh: 但如果这是一件大事，而且你无法与他人谈论，

sentences.en: your mind may return to it time and time again.
sentences.zh: 你的思绪可能会一次又一次地回到它上面。

sentences.en: And then it starts looking like the harm starts looking like a personal secrets harm.
sentences.zh: 然后，它造成的伤害看起来就和个人秘密造成的伤害一样了。

sentences.en: Is there something in the psychological makeup of somebody who can be a spy, for example, and can keep secrets and still perform every day?
sentences.zh: 在心理构成上，有没有人天生就能当间谍，既能保守秘密又能正常工作？

sentences.en: I mean, has anybody looked at that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，有人研究过这个问题吗？

sentences.en: I would say that someone who speaks their mind as soon as they have a thought would probably have a harder time in that job, or maybe never even make it close enough to find out.
sentences.zh: 我会说，那些一有想法就直言不讳的人，在那份工作中可能会更难受，或者根本没机会深入到那个地步。

sentences.en: Normally, when we have thoughts that there's people around, we share them.
sentences.zh: 通常，当我们周围有人时，有了想法我们就会分享。

sentences.en: And it's not just because we want people to know what's inside our head.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为我们想让别人知道我们在想什么。

sentences.en: It's just how we connect with people.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们与人建立联系的方式。

sentences.en: And it's also how we learn about the world.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们了解世界的方式。

sentences.en: You know, you share your thought and you see what someone says in response.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你分享了你的想法，然后看看别人的回应。

sentences.en: But if you have no trouble not sharing the thoughts that you're having, maybe, maybe you could be a spy.
sentences.zh: 但如果你对不分享自己的想法毫无压力，也许，也许你可以成为一名间谍。

sentences.en: Can, can we tell when people are keeping secrets?
sentences.zh: 我们能看出人们在保守秘密吗？

sentences.en: I know there's been research into whether somebody is lying, but are there giveaways when somebody is, is, you know, keeping some information from you?
sentences.zh: 我知道有人研究过某人是否在撒谎，但当某人，你知道，对你隐瞒信息时，会有什么迹象吗？

sentences.en: How would you know?
sentences.zh: 你怎么才能知道呢？

sentences.en: So in most situations, there's not any clues because people can't read your mind.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，没有任何线索，因为人们无法读懂你的心思。

sentences.en: They, they, they can understand if something's upsetting you or bothering you, but they can't literally see a secret on your face.
sentences.zh: 他们能看出你是否心烦意乱，但他们无法直接从你的脸上看出秘密。

sentences.en: And so, you know, in some ways that's great.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在某些方面这很好。

sentences.en: That's quite helpful that people can just read your secrets on your face.
sentences.zh: 如果人们能直接从你脸上读出秘密，那才叫麻烦。

sentences.en: That would be really frustrating.
sentences.zh: 那会让人非常沮丧。

sentences.en: Um, and so this, what the studies show is that when we bring two people together in a room and have one person hide something from the other, the other person can't
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以研究表明，当我们把两个人带到一个房间里，让其中一个人对另一个人隐瞒某事时，另一个人通常无法

sentences.en: tell that they're hiding something often.
sentences.zh: 察觉到他们在隐瞒什么。

sentences.en: Um, and people who watch the video recordings can't tell that they're hiding something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，观看录像的人也无法看出他们在隐瞒什么。

sentences.en: And so why, why is that the case?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: Intuitively, we'd think that maybe we would, people would somehow tell people would somehow be able to tell.
sentences.zh: 直觉上，我们可能会认为人们应该能以某种方式察觉出来。

sentences.en: Um, and I think when we think about that picture in our mind, we're sort of imagining the most difficult secrecy situation we can imagine
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想当我们想到那个画面时，我们是在想象我们能想到的最困难的保密情况，

sentences.en: someone asks you a question directly related to your secret.
sentences.zh: 有人直接问你与秘密相关的问题。

sentences.en: It turns out in real life, that doesn't happen very often.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在现实生活中，这种情况并不常发生。

sentences.en: Um, people don't go around asking people so much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们不会到处去问别人这些问题。

sentences.en: Have you ever cheated on your partner?
sentences.zh: 你有没有背叛过你的伴侣？

sentences.en: Were you ever abused during childhood?
sentences.zh: 你童年时期受过虐待吗？

sentences.en: These are just not questions we ask it.
sentences.zh: 这些根本不是我们会问的问题。

sentences.en: You know, these aren't topics that necessarily come up in conversation so much experiences of trauma.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些创伤经历并不一定会在谈话中出现。

sentences.en: And so those kinds of secrets, it's really hard to imagine how someone could somehow know that you're keeping them.
sentences.zh: 所以对于这类秘密，真的很难想象别人怎么可能知道你在保守它们。

sentences.en: Now, if it's your romantic partner, however, here's where things become different.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果是你的恋人，情况就不同了。

sentences.en: If there's a conversation topic that you're avoiding, which is one way, one frequent way folks try to
sentences.zh: 如果你在回避某个谈话话题，这是人们试图向恋人隐瞒秘密的一种常见方式，

sentences.en: keep secrets from their romantic partners, your partner's going to be able to tell.
sentences.zh: 你的伴侣是能察觉出来的。

sentences.en: Um, if there's just a conversation topic you'd ever seem to touch or sort of dodge, whenever it comes up, they're going to notice that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果有一个话题你从不触及，或者每当提到时就闪烁其词，他们会注意到的。

sentences.en: Um, and that is not going to be good.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那可不是什么好事。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, when we believe our partners are keeping secrets from us, one of the reasons that's so hurtful is we feel not included in their lives.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想，当我们认为伴侣对我们隐瞒秘密时，之所以会感到如此受伤，是因为我们觉得自己被排除在他们的生活之外了。

sentences.en: So you start your new book with a personal story about how you learned a significant family secret that your parents had kept from you on until well into your adulthood,
sentences.zh: 你新书的开头讲了一个个人故事，关于你是如何得知父母对你隐瞒了一个重大的家庭秘密，直到你成年很久之后，

sentences.en: when you were already doing research on the psychology of secrets.
sentences.zh: 那时你已经在研究秘密的心理学了。

sentences.en: Can you tell that story and how has that affected the work that you're doing now?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲那个故事吗？它对你现在的工作有什么影响？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So when I first started researching secrecy, I was doing it in a sort of strange way because I wasn't trying to learn about secrecy.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始研究保密性时，我的方式有点奇怪，因为我并不是想了解保密性本身。

sentences.en: I was trying to learn about metaphor, um, which you mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 我当时想了解的是隐喻，嗯，你之前提到过。

sentences.en: And secrecy was just one example of this idea that people describe secrets as heavy or weighty or burdensome.
sentences.zh: 而保密性只是人们将秘密描述为沉重、有分量或负担的这一概念的一个例子。

sentences.en: Um, I was just sort of interested in what secrets people associate with a sense of burden.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是对人们将哪些秘密与负担感联系在一起感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so I had been doing that research for a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 所以我做那项研究已经有几年了。

sentences.en: Um, and in fact, there was one particular day when I was giving my job talk to Columbia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，有一天我在哥伦比亚大学做求职演讲。

sentences.en: So I'm on my interview at Columbia for my position and I feel like it goes well.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在哥伦比亚大学面试我的职位，我觉得进展很顺利。

sentences.en: I present my research on, on secrecy to them.
sentences.zh: 我向他们展示了我的保密性研究。

sentences.en: And then later that night when I'm actually still with people from the interview, um, getting drinks at a bar,
sentences.zh: 那天晚上晚些时候，当我还在和面试人员一起在酒吧喝酒时，

sentences.en: I got a call from my dad and, you know, he never calls so, so late at night.
sentences.zh: 我接到了我爸爸的电话，你知道，他从来不会在深夜打电话。

sentences.en: And so I became really concerned.
sentences.zh: 所以我变得非常担心。

sentences.en: Something, something bad has happened and he called again and I'm like, Oh no.
sentences.zh: 出事了，他又打了一次，我想，噢不。

sentences.en: Um, you know, maybe there's been a death in the family or something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，也许家里有人去世了之类的。

sentences.en: And so I finally get in touch with him after the interview was officially over, said goodbye to everyone.
sentences.zh: 面试正式结束后，我告别了所有人，终于和他通上了话。

sentences.en: Um, and he says, Michael, I need to tell you something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他说，迈克尔，我需要告诉你一件事。

sentences.en: Uh, are you sitting down?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你坐下了吗？

sentences.en: And then he goes on to tell me, I didn't sit it down.
sentences.zh: 然后他接着告诉我，我没坐下。

sentences.en: Uh, he goes on to tell me that he's not biologically able to have children.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他接着告诉我，他在生理上无法生育。

sentences.en: He's is telling me that he's not my biological father.
sentences.zh: 他在告诉我，他不是我的亲生父亲。

sentences.en: And this is after a day of presenting my research on secrecy, uh, as part of this interview.
sentences.zh: 而这发生在我展示完保密性研究的那一天，作为面试的一部分。

sentences.en: And as you can imagine, that's very shocking to learn about.
sentences.zh: 正如你所能想象的，得知这一点非常令人震惊。

sentences.en: Um, but much later I realized essentially at the same time that my research was coming to this
sentences.zh: 嗯，但很久以后我意识到，基本上就在同一时间，我的研究得出了一个结论，

sentences.en: conclusion that it's not the act of hiding and conversation that's very difficult, but it's having to think about a secret and live with it alone in your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 即真正困难的不是在谈话中隐瞒的行为，而是必须思考一个秘密并独自在思想中与它共存。

sentences.en: Um, and I realized my parents situation was, was really a perfect illustration of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我意识到我父母的情况确实是一个完美的例证。

sentences.en: Um, because I had asked my parents much later, when did you decide to keep this secret?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我很久以后问过我父母，你们是什么时候决定保守这个秘密的？

sentences.en: Um, I assumed it was either after I was born shortly after I was born or shortly after my younger brother was born.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我以为是在我出生后不久，或者我弟弟出生后不久。

sentences.en: And my mom said, neither.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈说，都不是。

sentences.en: Um, we had decided that we would never tell our children and we could tell anyone else, but we would never tell our children.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们决定永远不告诉我们的孩子，我们可以告诉别人，但永远不会告诉我们的孩子。

sentences.en: And they decided that before we were ever born.
sentences.zh: 他们在我们出生前就决定了。

sentences.en: Um, and this is why secrecy, we really need to define it as an intention because the moment you intend to keep the secret, you have it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么我们需要将保密定义为一种意图，因为当你打算保守秘密的那一刻，你就已经拥有了它。

sentences.en: And they were keeping that they have the secret well before they could even hide it.
sentences.zh: 他们在甚至还没法隐瞒的时候就已经在保守这个秘密了。

sentences.en: Um, they could, it could already cast doubts and worries.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它已经可以引发怀疑和担忧了。

sentences.en: What if we looked different from my father or what they needed to know about our genetics?
sentences.zh: 如果我们看起来和我父亲不一样怎么办？或者关于我们的基因他们需要知道什么？

sentences.en: And so they told me that a lot of what was difficult about having that secret was not that they once in a while had to hide it in conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以他们告诉我，保守那个秘密最困难的部分并不是偶尔需要在谈话中隐瞒它。

sentences.en: That in fact was very rare, but they just had this once in a while, think about it and certain things would bring it back to the top of their minds.
sentences.zh: 事实上那非常罕见，但他们只是偶尔会想到它，某些事情会把它重新带回他们的脑海中。

sentences.en: And that is where the burden would come from.
sentences.zh: 这就是负担的来源。

sentences.en: And what precipitated your father's telling you when, when he told you, and did he know that this
sentences.zh: 那么是什么促使你父亲在你得知的时候告诉你？他知道这是对你很重要的一天，而且你刚刚结束了一场面试吗？

sentences.en: was an important day for you and that you would just finished an interview for a job?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以我了解到他们非常体贴地等面试结束后才告诉我。

sentences.en: So I learned that they could, they very considerably waited for the interview to be over.
sentences.zh: 不过他们那天想告诉我，因为可能在一两天前，我弟弟发现了这个秘密。

sentences.en: They wanted to tell me that day though, because maybe the day or two days before my brother had found out about the secret.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他发现的方式是他当时正在和我妈妈通电话。

sentences.en: Um, and the way he found out about it was he was on the, on a phone, on a phone call with my mom.
sentences.zh: 他们正在聊天。

sentences.en: They were chatting.
sentences.zh: 她随口提到她最近和她父亲，也就是我们的祖父吵了一架。

sentences.en: She mentioned offhandedly that she recently got in an argument with her father, our grandfather.
sentences.zh: 我弟弟说，那太奇怪了。

sentences.en: My brother was like, that's so weird.
sentences.zh: 我从来没听说过你们两个吵架。

sentences.en: I've never heard of you two arguing ever.
sentences.zh: 你们在吵什么？

sentences.en: What were you arguing about?
sentences.zh: 她说，我不能告诉你，这是一个秘密。

sentences.en: And she said, I can't tell you it's a secret.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，现在你必须告诉我了。

sentences.en: And he was like, well, now you have to tell me.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，我答应过我永远不会告诉你。

sentences.en: And she was like, no, I promised I would never tell you.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以想象，这确实是让别人不断追问直到他们得知秘密的好方法。

sentences.en: And so, as you can imagine, that's a great way to get someone to keep pushing and pushing until they, so they, until they learned the secret.
sentences.zh: 他确实做到了。

sentences.en: And he did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一旦他知道了，他们就必须让我知道，但他们想等面试结束后再告诉我。

sentences.en: Um, and once he learned it, they had to let me know, but they, they wanted to wait until the interview was over before they told me.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 那么接下来呢，关于秘密我们还需要知道什么？

sentences.en: So what, what next, what do we need to know about secrets?
sentences.zh: 你未来打算研究什么？

sentences.en: What are you looking into going forward?
sentences.zh: 在思考拥有一个秘密意味着什么以及你应该如何处理它时，

sentences.en: So in thinking about what it means to have a secret and what you should do with it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我们已经提到过的一点是，找第三方谈谈，

sentences.en: Um, you know, one thing that we've sort of alluded to already is talk to a third party, um, because they have a unique perspective that they can offer you.
sentences.zh: 因为他们能提供你所不具备的独特视角。

sentences.en: That's really hard to find on your own.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难独自找到。

sentences.en: And that's part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: When you're living alone with a secret, you're sort of stuck with your one way of thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 当你独自守着一个秘密生活时，你会被困在自己思考问题的方式中。

sentences.en: What we're doing now is starting to consider what the secrets are about.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在做的是开始考虑秘密的内容。

sentences.en: Um, and when I say there's
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我提到有38种秘密类别时，

sentences.en: 38 categories of secrets, that's too many categories for, for understanding like which secrets hurt you more than others.
sentences.zh: 对于理解哪些秘密比其他秘密更伤害你来说，类别太多了。

sentences.en: And so what we're doing now is understanding how people perceive their secrets as sort of compared to each other.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在正在做的是理解人们如何看待他们的秘密，以及它们之间的比较。

sentences.en: And it turns out that people see their secrets as having three primary dimensions, whether it's a secret to moral, whether it's secrets related to our relationships
sentences.zh: 事实证明，人们认为他们的秘密有三个主要维度：秘密是否涉及道德，秘密是否与我们的关系有关，

sentences.en: and whether it's secrets related to our goals, and trying to understand the unique qualities of those three different dimensions or experiences we can have with our secrets.
sentences.zh: 以及秘密是否与我们的目标有关，并试图理解这三个不同维度或我们可能拥有的秘密体验的独特品质。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for joining me today, Dr. Sleppian.
sentences.zh: 好的，感谢您今天参加我们的节目，斯莱皮安博士。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I promise I won't tell anyone what we talked about.
sentences.zh: 我保证不会告诉任何人我们谈论的内容。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。
